If a vCPU is outside guest mode and is scheduled out
process of making a memory access.  A problem occurs if another vCPU uses
the PV TLB flush feature during the period when the vCPU is scheduled
out
column2: and a virtual address has already been translated but has not yet

column1: been accessed
column2: because this is equivalent to using a stale TLB entry.

column1: To avoid this
column2: only report a vCPU as preempted if sure that the guest

column1: is at an instruction boundary.  A rescheduling request will be delivered
to the host physical CPU as an external interrupt
consider any vmexit *not* instruction boundary except for external
interrupts.
It would in principle be okay to report the vCPU as preempted also
if it is sleeping in kvm_vcpu_block(): a TLB flush IPI will incur the
vmentry/vmexit overhead unnecessarily
also unlikely to succeed.  However
column2: leave it for later because right

column1: now kvm_vcpu_check_block() is doing memory accesses.  Even
though the TLB flush issue only applies to virtual memory address
it's very much preferrable to be conservative.
